learning_outcomes.text: Have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects of computational fluid mechanics.
Have adequate knowledge of numerical simulation of industrial flows, including some knowledge at the forefront of the field in mechanical engineering.
Be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve problems of numerical simulation of industrial flows using established methods.
Be able to choose and apply different relevant discretization methods in computational fluid mechanics.
Be able to design and perform simulations of realistic industrial flow problems, interpret the data, and draw conclusions.
Be able to select and use appropriate numerical simulation software and computational equipment to solve numerical simulation problems of industrial flows.
Be able to combine fluid mechanics theory with computational techniques to solve fluid mechanics problems in the industrial field.
Understand the range of applicability and limitations of numerical simulation techniques for industrial flows.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
Adequate knowledge of their engineering branch, including some knowledge at the forefront of their field.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate, and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
The ability to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, and draw conclusions.
The ability to select and use appropriate equipment, tools, and methods.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds upon general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by elaborating and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Applied knowledge of the fundamentals of fluid mechanics systems and machines.

syllabus_topics: Basic equations of fluid mechanics. Levels of approximation.
Applications: use of a general-purpose commercial code (ANSYS FLUENT) for the implementation of a problem of industrial interest.
teaching_methods: In-class problem solving (in computer lab) of fluid dynamic problems representative of industrial flows
Completion of a final application project and submission of a report with results

assessment_methods.method: Participation in practical classes (effort and success in solving proposed cases, reflected in practice reports)
Final project (report evaluating clear presentation of problem and resolution method, and critical discussion of results)

assessment_rules: The evaluation is based on a mid-term exam (50%), participation in practical classes (15%), and a final project (35%).
bibliography: Jiyuan Tu, Guan Heng Yeoh y Chaoquin Liu. Computational Fluid Dymamics. A practical approach. Elsevier. 2008
Hirsch, C. Numerical Computation of Internal and External Flows (Second Edition). Elsevier. 2007
